atp-naming.statement: Advanced threat protection is the Go package advancedthreatsettings, with GetAdvancedThreatSettings, GetMaliciousURLs and GetSecurityExceptions, and the Python module atp_policy with ATPPolicyAPI.

go-has-python-catalog-services.statement: The Go SDK has packages for these ZIA services: risk profiles, sandbox rules, sub-clouds, extranet, ZPA gateways, proxies and dedicated IP gateways, proxy gateways, IPv6 configuration and NSS servers.

go-casb-and-custom-file-type-packages.statement: The Go SDK has packages for the SaaS Security CASB DLP rules (`/casbDlpRules`), CASB malware rules (`/casbMalwareRules`), custom file types (`/customFileTypes`) and DNS gateways (`/dnsGateways`).

go-dlp-resource-packages.statement: The Go DLP services include separate packages for ICAP servers (`/icapServers`), Incident Receiver servers (`/incidentReceiverServers`) and IDM profiles (`/idmprofile`, plus a `/lite` variant).

go-dedicated-ip-lite-only.statement: Go reads dedicated IP gateways through `GetDedicatedIPGWLite` in the forwarding-control `proxies` package, at `/dedicatedIPGateways/lite`.

go-gov-cloud-routing.statement: With cloud set to `gov` or `govus` (case-insensitive) the Go OneAPI client sends OAuth to the `zidentitygov.net` or `zidentitygov.us` domain under the vanity domain, and API calls to `https://api.zscalergov.net` or `https://api.zscalergov.us`.

july-services-unified-only.statement: The unified `ZIAService` registers DNS application groups, endpoint applications, Endpoint DLP rules, Outbound Email DLP rules, IPS categories and NSS collectors. The legacy ZIA client registers `web_dlp_global_options`.

july-lists-single-page.statement: The DNS application group, endpoint application and Outbound Email DLP rule list methods each send one request and build their results from `get_results()`, without a loop over further pages.

idm-profile-path.statement: The IDM profile calls use the `/idmprofile` path: Python `list_dlp_idm_profiles` and `get_dlp_idm_profiles`, the Go DLP IDM profile package, and the Automate capture all agree.

go-dedicated-ip-no-other-package.statement: No other Go ZIA package reads dedicated IP gateways; there is no standalone Go package for them.
go-dedicated-ip-no-other-package.conditions: A search of zscaler/zia in the Go SDK at the pin for `dedicatedIPGateways` finds only the proxies package; a search result, not a statement any source makes.

july-services-not-in-legacy.statement: The legacy ZIA client has no accessor for DNS application groups, endpoint applications, Endpoint DLP rules, Outbound Email DLP rules, IPS categories or NSS collectors.
july-services-not-in-legacy.conditions: A search of zscaler/zia/legacy.py at the pin for these accessor names finds none; a search result, not a statement any source makes. Release 1.9.39 (July 2026) added several of these services; IPS categories and NSS collectors are not in its notes.

go-no-config-audit.statement: The Go SDK has no service for `configAudit` or the System Audit Report.
go-no-config-audit.conditions: A search of zscaler/zia in the Go SDK at the pin for `configAudit` and `SystemAudit` finds nothing; a search result, not a statement any source makes.

parity-drift.title: Which ZIA modules exist in one SDK and not the other today
parity-drift.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The 2026-06-15 re-sweep named scim_api, eventlogentryreport, devicegroups-write and email_profiles as Go-only and said email_profiles had since reached Python; parity drifts release to release in both directions, whether any surface beyond the named ones changed was only spot-checked, and the module diff of the Go services tree against the Python zia tree has not been run exhaustively. Clarification zia-51.
parity-drift.blocks: Choosing between the Go and Python SDKs for a ZIA surface.

device-groups-write.title: Whether the ZIA device-groups API accepts group-level writes
device-groups-write.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Python's device-groups clients only read, and the legacy note treated group writes as a Go-only capability; the Go package at the pin is read-only too, so no SDK wraps a group write, and whether the underlying API supports one is not source-verifiable from the SDK layer. Clarification zia-51.
device-groups-write.blocks: Whether a device group can be created or changed through the API at all.

prose.text: SDK presence is a statement about code, not about whether a tenant can use the endpoint. The Go and Python SDKs do not wrap the same ZIA endpoints, and the difference moves with each release.

checks.do: Which SDK carries the surface before choosing a client, by listing the module trees at the pinned versions rather than trusting an old list.
Whether a device-group write is needed; neither SDK wraps one, so it would be a direct API call.
Whether the Go SDK has a package for a service before concluding it is Python-only, because several services once listed as Python-only exist in Go.
That a coverage claim rests on the SDK code and not on a release note, since both changelogs omit endpoints the code implements.
Which client class the script built before expecting a July 2026 accessor to exist on it.
Whether a list result from one of the newer services could be a partial page.
Whether a Shadow IT export by entity passes the literal USER or LOCATION.
That VIP lookups go through the GRE tunnel accessor and datacenter lookups through the datacenters accessor.
